title: How To Be A Better, Happier Teacher Next School Year hool-year/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: As the school year ends, Linsin offers a self-assessment survey built around fourteen core SCM principles, asking teachers to rate themselves 1-5 on items like consistently following their management plan, avoiding external rewards, and building rapport with difficult students. He frames the exercise as a private, brutally honest reflection tool meant to pinpoint what stood in the way of loving the job during the past year. He notes the fourteen principles work synergistically, so even a small improvement in one area — like consistency — tends to strengthen the others. The article closes with pointers to the SCM archive and Linsin's four books for readers wanting deeper explanation of any surveyed item, alongside an invitation for topic requests.
points: The article provides a fourteen-item self-assessment survey covering core SCM principles like consistency, praise, rapport, and stress levels.
The survey is meant to be private and brutally honest, used to pinpoint what got in the way of loving the job during the past year.
The fourteen principles reinforce each other synergistically, so improving one (e.g., consistency) tends to strengthen the rest.
Readers are pointed to the SCM archive and Linsin's book catalog for deeper explanation of any surveyed principle.
quotes: Because, unless you know where you need to improve, you’re destined to experience the same frustrations year after year.
So I created a survey based on the core principles and philosophies of SCM.
I recommend giving yourself a score between one and five to represent the degree in which you’re able to answer yes for each item.
I refrained from lecturing, scolding, yelling, glaring, or using any other form of intimidation.
It’s important to point out that the principles listed in the survey are in large part dependent on one another.
It means that even a small change, like becoming more consistent, can improve the other areas as well.
This is no pie-in-the-sky scenario. Our approach has been proven over and over again with thousands of teachers around the world.
